reason: The branching airways end beside the sacs, so joining them should start the air route.
expectation: The airways and sacs will form a connected route for air.

effect: The air route is built, and its empty exchange-surface slot suggests adding the thin lining next.
reaction: The comparison of small sacs with one large space makes the surface-area advantage clear.
reason: The thin exchange lining forms the air-facing side of the sac wall, so it fits the available slot.
expectation: The lining will be fitted to the air sacs as part of the exchange surface.

effect: The lining is in place, and the result identifies the capillary mesh as the next missing part.
reaction: The picture makes the two sides of the exchange surface easy to follow.
reason: The capillary mesh surrounds the sacs and supplies the blood-facing side of the exchange surface.
expectation: The capillaries will be added around the lined air sacs to form an exchange surface.

effect: The lung route now has an exchange surface, so it can be connected to the blood circuit.
reaction: The separate arrows make the exchange between air and blood clear.
reason: The lung capillaries need to connect to the circulating blood to carry oxygen onward.
expectation: The lung exchange surface will join the blood circuit.

effect: The blood circuit now reaches the lung capillaries, but the air must be renewed to maintain oxygen exchange.
reaction: The shrinking oxygen arrows clarify why circulation alone is not enough.
reason: The pleural membranes connect the lung side to the moving chest, so they appear to be the next part needed for breathing.
expectation: The membranes will attach to the lung route and prepare it to move with the chest.

effect: The pleura now covers the lung and can connect it to the moving chest.
reaction: The coupling gives the membranes a clear role in breathing.
reason: The breathing chest can couple to the outer pleural sheet and renew air in the sacs.
expectation: Chest movement will expand the lungs and renew the air reaching the exchange surface.

effect: The moving chest completed the oxygen-delivering circulation, connecting renewed lung air to oxygen delivery at tissues.
reaction: The complete route was satisfying to see, especially how it connected breathing to distant cells.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the lung route to the blood circuit was most worthwhile: the result showed why blood flow needs renewed air to keep oxygen exchange going.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the lining and capillary mesh separately felt somewhat repetitive, though the pictures distinguished the air-facing and blood-facing sides.

surprise.text: The shrinking oxygen arrows changed my understanding of why circulation alone is insufficient when the air in the sacs stays still.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary. The pleural membranes were less familiar, but their picture and the later coupling to the chest gave them a purpose.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the sequence made me curious about how other body systems supply working cells, although the direct assembly steps became predictable.
